criteria.text: Adults with severe hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency with factor VIII activity <1 IU/dL) without pre-existing AAV5 antibodies detected by an FDA-approved test (FDA indication; approval criterion 3).
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a hematologist (approval criterion 2).
Moderate to severe disease as defined by factor VIII levels <1 IU/dL (approval criterion 4).
More than 150 previous exposure days to factor VIII (approval criterion 5).
No history of factor VIII inhibitors AND negative screen <0.6 Bethesda units within two weeks prior to administration (approval criterion 6).
No pre-existing antibodies to AAV5 detected by an FDA-approved test (approval criterion 7; FDA indication).
Hepatic ultrasound AND elastography performed prior to administration (approval criterion 8a).
Baseline liver function tests ALT, AST, GGT, ALP, total bilirubin, and INR documented (approval criterion 8b).
No current active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection (denial criterion 2).
No current uncontrolled HIV infection (denial criterion 3).
No known hepatic fibrosis stage 3 or 4 or cirrhosis (denial criterion 4).
No known hypersensitivity to mannitol (denial criterion 5).
No previous gene therapy for hemophilia A (denial criterion 6).

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Roctavian (valoctocogene roxaparvovec-rvox), an AAV vector-based gene therapy for adults with severe hemophilia A. Version: 1; Original: 07/3/2023; Accepted: 09/15/2023; Effective: 11/1/2023.
Encoded: FDA indication, approval criteria 1-8 and denial exclusions 2-6. Denial criterion 1 (failure to meet approval criteria) is covered by the approval clauses.
Duration (notes only): initial approval 3 months; no reauthorization will be approved.
Quantity (notes only): one infusion per lifetime; HCPCS J3590. No numeric quantity enforcement; max_units is null.
Cautions (notes only): thromboembolic events may occur with elevated factor VIII activity above the upper limit of normal.

Cautions (notes only): patients with preexisting hepatocellular carcinoma risk factors should receive regular alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) monitoring and abdominal ultrasound screenings for five years following administration.

Cautions (notes only): monitor ALT weekly for at least 26 weeks after administration and institute corticosteroid treatment for elevations as required; continue ALT monitoring until baseline. Monitor factor VIII activity with ALT because ALT elevations may accompany decreased factor VIII activity.

Remaining gaps: documentation verification, duration, no reauthorization, lifetime quantity enforcement and post-dose monitoring require manual review. Clinical findings, exposure days, testing, imaging and baseline labs are attestations; no numeric liver lab thresholds are specified.
PDL status unknown. No evaluate-linked alternatives: hemophilia B peers are not alternatives for this hemophilia A indication.
